reference: Bash metadata and the documented concise signature-list contract. Synthetic regular files encode filesystem magic offsets independently; util-linux wipefs is used only for empty/unmatched-file CLI comparisons, since its detailed signature validation and row format differ.
coverage: Bash reports wipefs as a builtin with the executable search path disabled by the runner.
Bash help registration and the loadable's published synopsis are checked.
The command's own --help output is checked against its published help text.
Future safe inspection, dry-run, and erase behavior is specified as deferred work with independent reference requirements.
Read-only listing and -n/--no-act on independently encoded private regular files; missing operands and aggregate continuation.
exclusions: Raw devices and actual -a erasure remain deferred to a disposable VM or reviewed pwrite mock.
The concise offset/type/path rows are a custom contract, not full util-linux probing parity.
Bash type/help and command help/version cases are metadata only and do not count as operation coverage.

cases.purpose: Verify Bash resolves the loadable as a builtin when candidate execution uses an empty PATH.
Verify Bash has registered help for wipefs; the marker makes the expected output independent of help formatting.
Check Bash's short-help form against the usage synopsis declared in the builtin table entry.
Check wipefs --help prints the documented mode descriptions and signature-family scope without opening a target.
cases.stdout:
Detect or wipe filesystem / swap signatures.

    wipefs device       list detected signatures (offset, type)
    wipefs -a device    erase all detected signatures
    wipefs -n device    dry-run: show what -a would erase

Recognises swap, ext, xfs, btrfs, ntfs, vfat and iso9660 magics.

cases.purpose: List an independently encoded XFS magic at offset zero using default and read-only dry-run modes; verify the complete input remains unchanged.
cases.script:
printf 'XFSBfixture' > image
wipefs image
wipefs -n image
wipefs --no-act image
[[ $(<image) == XFSBfixture ]]
cases.stdout:
0x0	xfs	image
0x0	xfs	image
0x0	xfs	image

cases.purpose: Qualify -a byte changes, including multiple signatures and preservation of unrelated fixture data.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r5: unchanged: needs a block device node

cases.purpose: Empty and unmatched private regular files are silent and unchanged in both independent util-linux and candidate runs.
cases.script:
: > empty
printf 'ordinary bytes\n' > plain
wipefs empty plain

cases.purpose: List two independently encoded magic offsets in one bounded regular file and verify all bytes with an independent Python byte oracle.
cases.script:
{ printf 'XFSB'; printf '%1076s' ''; printf '\123\357'; printf 'tail'; } > image
wipefs -n image
/usr/bin/python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
assert Path('image').read_bytes() == b'XFSB'+b' '*1076+b'\x53\xef'+b'tail'
PY

cases.purpose: A missing private operand fails overall while later regular-file inspection still emits its signature.
cases.script:
printf XFSB > image
wipefs absent image
